title: Axor Lab Experiment
description: Binds what runs to how it's observed: a scenario/bench set, repeats, the agent artifact, the experiment type, and OPTIONALLY the conditions to compare. Conditions live HERE, not in a scenario — the same scenario is reused across conditions. An experiment with no `conditions` is a single-arm run (just execute the agent and observe); governance is a capability an experiment opts into by declaring conditions, never a requirement (Suite Platform RFC §10).

bench_id.description: optional: an ordered bench instead of a loose scenario set

suite_ref.description: the suite/v1 manifest this experiment was resolved from (id or content hash). Absent for a hand-authored experiment that no suite produced.

conditions.description: OPTIONAL. Omit for a single-arm run (the agent is executed and observed, no enforcement axis). 1 condition pins one configuration explicitly; ≥2 compares, and each must differ in exactly the axis under study. A comparison claim (comparison_design, a paired test, the Control Plane bridge) requires ≥2 — that is enforced where the claim is made, not here.

repeats.description: n per condition; statistics.md governs the unit of analysis

comparison_design.description: how the two conditions are compared. matched_pairs (McNemar) is valid ONLY when the agent's behavior is fixed by scenario+seed (a deterministic/replayed agent). A live model is sampled independently per condition → independent_samples (a two-proportion comparison, reported as exploratory). If omitted, the design is inferred from the agent.
